claim_policy: These are Phase 06 manuscript-authoring claims, not finished prose. Each claim is scoped to what its sources can establish. Reported paper results must retain experimental conditions; official documentation supports current interfaces only; Mosaic examples remain synthetic and cannot imply company outcomes.

chapters.title: The Model Is Not the Behavior

claims.statement: A model response is one observation from a configured system, not proof of dependable product behavior.
claims.limitations: Accountability model synthesized across lifecycle and evaluation evidence.

claims.statement: Evaluation must be designed into development because model outputs and versions can vary.
claims.limitations: No evaluation set is complete.

claims.statement: Technical controls and documentation do not transfer formal risk or domain authority to the LLM engineer.
claims.limitations: Organization-specific decision rights must be documented.

claims.statement: Success criteria should specify task, inputs, outputs, failure behavior, consequence, and judgment method before model optimization.
claims.limitations: Contract fields are a book synthesis, not a standard.

claims.statement: Representative language and consequence segments are required because aggregate performance can hide important failures.
claims.limitations: Segment choice remains use-case specific.

claims.statement: Human review is a designed authority/control relationship, not a generic safety guarantee.
claims.limitations: Reviewer competence, workload, and decision rights require local evidence.

chapters.title: Reason About Tokens, Attention, and Generation

claims.statement: Transformer generation conditions each next token on represented prior context through attention-based layers.
claims.limitations: Modern architectures contain additional mechanisms and variants.

claims.statement: Subword tokenization changes sequence length and representation, with language- and domain-specific effects.
claims.limitations: Effects must be measured with the actual tokenizer.

claims.statement: Decoding and chat-template configuration are part of behavior identity and must be versioned.
claims.limitations: Library defaults and model templates change.

chapters.title: Select a Model and Access Posture

claims.statement: Public benchmark or scale alone cannot establish fitness for a specific task and deployment posture.
claims.limitations: Model comparison criteria remain task specific.

claims.statement: Managed and weight-access paths expose different control, inspection, hosting, adaptation, and operational surfaces.
claims.limitations: Provider terms and supported controls are volatile.

claims.statement: Model lifecycle/deprecation risk should be treated as an architecture input before release.
claims.limitations: One provider's schedule illustrates, not standardizes, lifecycle practice.

claims.statement: A reproducible behavior baseline identifies model, prompt/messages, context, decoding, schema, evaluator, and runtime configuration.
claims.limitations: Hardware/provider nondeterminism can prevent bitwise reproduction.

claims.statement: Repeated trials are needed when stochastic behavior can affect the decision.
claims.limitations: Trial count depends on variance and decision consequence.

claims.statement: A deterministic test double verifies software contracts but cannot establish live-model quality.
claims.limitations: Engineering testing inference; not stated verbatim by sources.

claims.statement: Instructions, examples, delimiters, message roles, and templates are configuration surfaces whose effects must be evaluated.
claims.limitations: Guidance varies across model families.

claims.statement: Untrusted retrieved or user content can carry indirect instructions that conflict with application intent.
claims.limitations: Attack success and defenses evolve.

claims.statement: Prompt instructions alone are not evidence of an effective security or safety control.
claims.limitations: Required layered controls depend on risk context.

claims.statement: Schema-constrained generation can improve syntactic conformance to supported JSON Schema.
claims.limitations: Supported schema subset and model behavior are provider specific.

claims.statement: Syntactic validity does not establish factual correctness, permission, provenance, or authorization.
claims.limitations: Requires local semantic validators and authority design.

claims.statement: Abstention, escalation, repair, and fail-closed behavior should be explicit product states rather than improvised prose.
claims.limitations: State model is the book's engineering pattern.

claims.statement: Context-window capacity does not guarantee equal or reliable use of information at every position.
claims.limitations: Magnitude varies with current model and task.

claims.statement: Longer context can increase input cost and latency, so selection and caching choices require workload measurement.
claims.limitations: Pricing and caching semantics change.

claims.statement: Truncation, conflict, staleness, and authorization are distinct context failure states.
claims.limitations: Exact controls depend on source-system metadata.

claims.statement: Retrieval is justified only when external evidence ownership, freshness, or coverage materially improves the task.
claims.limitations: Decision rule is task specific.

claims.statement: Relevance does not establish source authority, permission, currency, or answerability.
claims.limitations: Metadata and authority design are organization specific.

claims.statement: A retrieval-grounded system needs independent retrieval and generated-behavior claims.
claims.limitations: Metric choices remain bounded.

chapters.title: Build the Retrieval and Reranking Path

claims.statement: Sparse, dense, and late-interaction retrieval expose different effectiveness and resource tradeoffs.
claims.limitations: No method dominates all corpora and queries.

claims.statement: Chunking, metadata filters, candidate retrieval, and reranking are separately diagnosable stages.
claims.limitations: Chunking evidence is corpus/model specific.

claims.statement: Synthetic hypothetical-document retrieval is an experimental option, not a truth or grounding guarantee.
claims.limitations: May import generator assumptions and costs.

claims.statement: Retrieved evidence should retain source identity and citation targets through context assembly.
claims.limitations: Citation feature availability and granularity vary.

claims.statement: Supporting, conflicting, stale, absent, and unauthorized evidence require different behavior.
claims.limitations: Behavior contract and owner decisions remain local.

claims.statement: Context ordering and position can affect use, so packing policy needs direct evaluation.
claims.limitations: Current model-specific testing required.

claims.statement: End-to-end RAG quality can fail at corpus, query, retrieval, ranking, context, generation, citation, or evaluation layers.
claims.limitations: Layer taxonomy is adapted for this book.

claims.statement: Retrieval metrics and generated-answer metrics answer different questions and should not be collapsed prematurely.
claims.limitations: Automated generation metrics require calibration.

claims.statement: Groundedness or faithfulness metrics do not prove source truth or organizational authority.
claims.limitations: Terminology differs across tools and papers.

claims.statement: Evaluation cases need documented provenance, segments, coverage, exclusions, split identity, and refresh policy.
claims.limitations: No documentation proves representativeness alone.

claims.statement: Duplicate or contaminated cases can inflate apparent generalization and invalidate comparisons.
claims.limitations: Overlap detection is imperfect.

claims.statement: Multilingual coverage requires direct per-language/task evidence rather than an English aggregate.
claims.limitations: Language coverage in cited work does not transfer automatically.

claims.statement: Criteria, error category, consequence, severity, detectability, segment, and disposition are distinct evaluation fields.
claims.limitations: Book taxonomy is not a standard.

claims.statement: LLM judges can exhibit position, verbosity, and self-preference biases.
claims.limitations: Biases and magnitude vary by judge/task.

claims.statement: Model graders should be calibrated against credible human or domain judgments and retain disagreement/limitations.
claims.limitations: Human/domain judgments can also be inconsistent.

claims.statement: A causal model-system claim needs a baseline, explicit hypothesis, controlled variable family, repeated trials where relevant, and decision criteria.
claims.limitations: Some production changes cannot be perfectly isolated.

claims.statement: Aggregate gains should not erase segment regressions or uncertainty.
claims.limitations: Statistical treatment depends on sample/process.

claims.statement: An experiment should end in retain, revise, reject, scope, or release disposition rather than score collection alone.
claims.limitations: Disposition vocabulary is book-specific.

chapters.title: Release, Observe, and Change the Model

claims.statement: Release evidence spans behavior, reliability, latency/cost, privacy/security controls, owners, observability, and rollback.
claims.limitations: Formal release gates are organization specific.

claims.statement: Model/provider migration requires replay of frozen task evidence and recording changed limitations.
claims.limitations: Provider deprecation is an illustration, not the only change trigger.

claims.statement: Adaptation is justified only after residual failures survive simpler task, context, retrieval, prompt, schema, and evaluation repairs.
claims.limitations: Intervention order is evidence dependent.

chapters.title: Start From a Frozen Behavior Baseline

claims.statement: An adaptation claim is interpretable only against a frozen behavior/configuration/evaluation baseline.
claims.limitations: Frozen means versioned, not permanently immutable.

claims.statement: Target gains, retained capabilities, controls, resource budgets, and rejection criteria should precede training.
claims.limitations: Criteria remain task specific.

claims.statement: Upstream defects must be ruled out before attributing a failure to model weights.
claims.limitations: Causal isolation can remain uncertain.

chapters.title: Inspect the Model and Tokenizer Boundary

claims.statement: Tokenizer, template, architecture, position/context mechanism, precision, and checkpoint are separate model-system surfaces.
claims.limitations: Specific model internals must come from its primary documentation/code.

claims.statement: Token fragmentation can change effective sequence length and multilingual/domain representation.
claims.limitations: Requires actual tokenizer measurements.

claims.statement: Architecture inspection identifies plausible intervention surfaces but cannot predict task improvement without experiments.
claims.limitations: Mechanistic inference is deliberately bounded.

claims.statement: Prompt/context repair, SFT, PEFT, preference optimization, distillation, continued pretraining, and model replacement target different failure hypotheses.
claims.limitations: Methods may overlap; selection is not a fixed ladder.

claims.statement: Weight access, data quality, compute, reversibility, runtime, and control requirements constrain available interventions.
claims.limitations: Resource claims are implementation specific.

claims.statement: At least one plausible intervention should be rejected using predicted evidence or boundary constraints before experimentation expands.
claims.limitations: Engineering discipline derived from evaluation principles.

claims.statement: A data recipe identifies sources, rights/permissions, example schema, inclusion/exclusion, quality, mixture, transformations, reviewers, versions, and limitations.
claims.limitations: Recipe completeness does not prove lawful use or representativeness.

claims.statement: Synthetic instruction data can scale examples but may reproduce generator errors and biases.
claims.limitations: Quality depends on generation/filter/review configuration.

claims.statement: Multilingual mixtures need explicit language/task balance and separate evaluation.
claims.limitations: No universal optimal mixture.

claims.statement: Deduplication can reduce memorization and evaluation contamination but thresholds and scope create tradeoffs.
claims.limitations: Near-duplicate detection is imperfect and corpus dependent.

claims.statement: Train, development, evaluation, retention, and control sets need explicit separation and identity.
claims.limitations: Historical pretraining overlap may be unknowable for managed/base models.

claims.statement: Filtering and normalization choices alter the learned distribution and must be recorded as data decisions.
claims.limitations: Effects need target experiments.

claims.statement: Instruction examples must map to target behavior clauses, errors, and segments rather than convenience prompts.
claims.limitations: Coverage rubric is task specific.

claims.statement: Chat template and loss masking determine which tokens contribute to SFT learning.
claims.limitations: Trainer/template support is version specific.

claims.statement: Negative, abstention, and boundary cases are needed when the contract requires non-answer behavior.
claims.limitations: Examples do not guarantee generalization.

claims.statement: Preference data encodes a rubric, rater population, presentation order, and collection process rather than objective truth.
claims.limitations: Some tasks have objective criteria that can supplement preference.

claims.statement: Position, verbosity, style, and self-preference biases can affect pairwise judgments.
claims.limitations: Bias magnitude varies.

claims.statement: Implicit production feedback is confounded by exposure, interface, incentives, and user selection unless designed as credible evidence.
claims.limitations: Needs product-specific causal design.

claims.statement: Adaptation promotion requires target improvement plus retention, segment, and control regression evidence.
claims.limitations: Protected suite is never exhaustive.

claims.statement: Language/domain gains can coexist with regressions outside the target mixture.
claims.limitations: Observed transfer/regression patterns vary.

claims.statement: Safety/control cases and accountable owners must be preserved through adaptation rather than assumed from the base model.
claims.limitations: Formal acceptance remains external.

claims.statement: A training run manifest needs base/tokenizer, data/splits, objective, optimizer/schedule, batch/sequence, precision, seeds, code, hardware class, checkpoints, and evaluators.
claims.limitations: Nondeterminism can remain.

claims.statement: Mixed precision and sharding change memory/communication behavior and checkpoint procedures.
claims.limitations: PyTorch version/hardware specific.

claims.statement: Training loss and resource completion do not establish target behavior improvement.
claims.limitations: Behavior evaluators also have limitations.

claims.statement: SFT optimizes likelihood on selected training tokens and therefore depends critically on data/template/masking choices.
claims.limitations: Exact objective/configuration varies.

claims.statement: Checkpoint selection should use held-out target, retention, segment, control, and resource evidence rather than minimum training loss.
claims.limitations: Selection policy is task specific.

claims.statement: Synthetic and multilingual training gains require independent held-out evaluation.
claims.limitations: Cited studies do not validate Mosaic.

claims.statement: LoRA introduces trainable low-rank updates while freezing base weights, reducing trainable parameter/storage burden under studied conditions.
claims.limitations: Quality and efficiency vary by target modules/rank/model/task.

claims.statement: PEFT method support differs for layers, quantized bases, merging, hotswap, and runtime behavior.
claims.limitations: Fast-moving library support.

claims.statement: An efficient adaptation must still pass the same target, retention, control, and inference compatibility evidence.
claims.limitations: No universal acceptable regression threshold.

claims.statement: DPO optimizes a preference objective relative to a reference behavior without a separately trained explicit reward model in its original formulation.
claims.limitations: Implementation variants and assumptions differ.

claims.statement: Preference optimization can overfit biased or shortcut-bearing judgments, so independent behavior and retention evaluation is required.
claims.limitations: Failure mechanisms are data/objective/model specific.

claims.statement: Using the same model family to generate preferences, train, and judge can create coupled evidence that must be disclosed and independently checked.
claims.limitations: Independence is graded, not binary.

chapters.title: Decide on Distillation or Continued Pretraining

claims.statement: Distillation transfers teacher behavior into a student under an explicit objective and data process; it is not generic compression magic.
claims.limitations: Modern generative distillation has additional failure surfaces.

claims.statement: Continued pretraining targets domain/task distribution through additional unsupervised language modeling and carries contamination/retention costs.
claims.limitations: Older study architecture differs from current decoder LLMs.

claims.statement: Advanced adaptation should be rejected when its hypothesis, data, resource, or evaluation burden is not distinct from a smaller intervention.
claims.limitations: Decision rule belongs to this book.

chapters.title: Package and Version the Model System

claims.statement: Deployable identity must bind base/checkpoint, tokenizer/template, adapter, config, schema, runtime, provenance/license, and integrity metadata.
claims.limitations: No universal manifest standard is claimed.

claims.statement: Model cards document intended use, evaluation, and limitations but do not approve deployment.
claims.limitations: Document quality varies.

claims.statement: Artifact format and checksums improve integrity/handling but do not prove provenance or behavioral compatibility.
claims.limitations: Supply-chain controls require broader evidence.

chapters.title: Reason About Inference Memory and Throughput

claims.statement: Inference memory includes weights plus runtime state such as KV cache whose size depends on model, sequence, precision, and batch/concurrency.
claims.limitations: Exact formulas depend on architecture/runtime.

claims.statement: Prefill and decode phases have different compute/memory behavior, and batching/caching/routing alter throughput and tail latency.
claims.limitations: Workload/runtime/hardware specific.

claims.statement: Task-level capacity models should record hardware/runtime/configuration and escalate kernel/platform work to adjacent specialists.
claims.limitations: Role boundary is architecture-derived.

claims.statement: Quantization can reduce memory/compute cost but its quality and speed effects depend on method, model, calibration, hardware, and runtime.
claims.limitations: Paper/vendor metrics are not Mosaic evidence.

claims.statement: Paged KV management, batching, caching, and speculative decoding can improve serving efficiency under bounded workloads.
claims.limitations: Benefit can reverse under different load/batch/model combinations.

claims.statement: Serving configuration must be selected on a measured behavior-resource frontier including protected segments and latency tails.
claims.limitations: Frontier expires with workload/version changes.

chapters.title: Release, Diagnose, and Evolve Adapted Models

claims.statement: Adapted-model release needs target, retention, control, runtime, owner, observability, cohort, and rollback evidence.
claims.limitations: Release authority and cohort design are local.

claims.statement: Incident diagnosis must distinguish data, checkpoint/adapter, tokenizer/template, evaluator, runtime, and infrastructure changes.
claims.limitations: Some failures cross layers.

claims.statement: A correction is incomplete until evidence, tests, controls, manifests, limitations, and monitoring are updated and replayed.
claims.limitations: Organizational incident process remains adjacent.
